checks.name: Independent price source (Coinbase)
checks.detail: Coinbase agreed on direction in 98.9% of 90 sampled windows and 100.0% of those that finished $2.00+ from the line (under $1.00: 23/24; $1.00–2.00: 16/16; $2.00–4.00: 23/23; $4.00+: 27/27). Disagreement near the line is expected: Coinbase is one exchange, the index averages several. 10 windows had no candles.

checks.name: Runs test (is the sequence random?)
checks.detail: 16,508 runs vs 15,835 expected (z = +7.57, p = 0.000): more switches than chance: results tend to alternate. Check that it also holds out of sample.

checks.name: Does one result predict the next?
checks.detail: lag-1 correlation -0.0425 (z = -7.57). Statistically non-zero, but check its size: a correlation this small moves the next window's odds by only about 2.1 percentage points, less than fees cost.

checks.name: Hour-of-day lean holds out of sample?
checks.detail: Split at 2026-05-31. Hours that looked significant in the first half: 18:00; still significant, same direction, in the second half: 18:00. Correlation of hourly leans between halves: +0.44 (some persistence; worth watching).

checks.name: Streak behaviour holds out of sample?
checks.detail: after 3 Ups the next was Up 43.7% (first half, n=1,663) vs 46.7% (second half, n=1,787); after 3 Downs the next was Up 57.0% (first half, n=1,697) vs 54.6% (second half, n=1,795). For a fade-or-follow rule to pay, the same lean must show in both halves and be larger than the ~2–3¢ per contract that spread and fees cost.

checks.name: Kalshi price edge holds out of sample?
checks.detail: No price level was clearly profitable after fees. 7 more showed a paper profit that sits inside its error band, so it could just be luck: buy Yes at 80–90¢: +4.9¢ ±5.7 (n=89); buy Yes at 60–70¢: +2.7¢ ±13.0 (n=50); buy No at 20–30¢: +1.0¢ ±9.5 (n=74). Most windows trade under 10¢ or over 90¢; there, recent results ran -0.7¢ to +0.3¢ per contract.

checks.name: Chance findings to expect
checks.detail: The report tests 35 hour, weekday and slot groups; at 95% confidence about 1.8 would look significant by luck alone. Found: 3. That's no more than luck would produce.
